questions.question: What is climate?
choices: Conditions at one place during a single afternoon
Long-term patterns of weather in a region
Only the temperature at noon
Only the total rain in one storm

questions.question: What is weather?
choices: Long-term average conditions over decades
The location of continents
The distribution of soil types
Short-term atmospheric conditions

questions.question: Which factor most directly affects the angle of sunlight reaching a region?
choices: Latitude
Population density
Political borders
Language

questions.question: How does temperature generally change with increasing elevation in the lower atmosphere?
choices: It increases at the same rate everywhere
It remains identical at every elevation
It decreases
It becomes unrelated to altitude

questions.question: What is precipitation?
choices: The movement of tectonic plates
Water falling from the atmosphere as rain, snow, or other forms
The upward movement of molten rock
The erosion of coastlines by tides

questions.question: What is a rain shadow?
choices: A drier area on the leeward side of a mountain range
A wetland formed by river flooding
A region shaded by tall city buildings
A zone defined by constant ocean fog

questions.question: What is the greenhouse effect?
choices: Cooling caused by all sunlight being reflected
Heating caused only by volcanoes
Cooling caused by ocean tides
Warming caused by gases absorbing and re-emitting outgoing infrared energy

questions.question: Why do coastal places often have milder temperatures than inland places at similar latitude?
choices: Coasts always receive less sunlight
Ocean water prevents all temperature changes
Water heats and cools more slowly than land
Every coastal location has the same elevation

questions.question: How can ocean currents affect climate?
choices: They redistribute heat and influence nearby conditions
They determine political borders
They eliminate seasonal change worldwide
They stop atmospheric circulation

questions.question: Why does the windward side of a mountain often receive more precipitation?
choices: Descending air always gains moisture from rocks
Rising moist air cools and water vapor condenses
Mountains generate water without atmospheric moisture
Windward slopes receive no solar energy

questions.question: What causes Earth's seasons primarily?
choices: Large changes in the sun's size each month
Daily changes in Earth's rotation direction
The moon blocking sunlight each winter
Earth's axial tilt as it orbits the sun

questions.question: Why are the tropics generally warmer than polar regions?
choices: They are always closer to the sun than any other region
They contain no clouds
They receive more direct solar energy over the year
They have no nighttime hours

questions.question: How does increased greenhouse gas concentration affect Earth's energy balance?
choices: It reduces heat loss to space until a warmer balance develops
It blocks every form of incoming sunlight
It removes all water vapor from the atmosphere
It prevents oceans from absorbing heat

questions.question: Why is one unusually cold day insufficient to disprove long-term warming?
choices: Cold days cannot occur during winter
Weather varies over short periods while climate describes longer patterns
Climate depends only on one city's temperature
Long-term records never include daily observations

questions.question: Why do climate classifications consider precipitation as well as temperature?
choices: Temperature has no effect on ecosystems
Precipitation determines latitude
Every region has identical rainfall
Moisture patterns influence environments alongside heat

questions.question: A town east of a mountain range is dry while prevailing winds arrive from the west. Which process may explain this?
choices: A volcanic eruption
A change in longitude alone
A rain shadow
A coastal tide

questions.question: Two cities share a latitude, but one lies at high elevation. Which is generally expected, other factors equal?
choices: The higher city is cooler
Both cities must have identical temperatures
The higher city is always wetter
The lower city has no seasonal variation

questions.question: Which evidence is most useful for studying a long-term climate trend?
choices: One afternoon's temperature
Consistent measurements collected over many decades
A single photograph of a snowstorm
One week's tourist reservations

questions.question: A coastal city has smaller seasonal temperature changes than an inland city at similar latitude. What is a likely explanation?
choices: Latitude changes daily at the coast
The coast receives no winter sunlight
The inland city has no atmospheric pressure
The ocean moderates temperature

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes climate from weather?
choices: Today's rain describes climate; a thirty-year average describes weather
Both terms describe only extreme storms
A thirty-year rainfall average describes climate; today's rain describes weather
Neither term includes precipitation
